newsitem.title: JAPAN: More Japan financial failures possible -- BOJ.
newsitem.headline: More Japan financial failures possible -- BOJ.

text.p: More failures of Japanese financial institutions cannot be ruled out, Tadayo Honma, executive director at the Bank of Japan (BOJ), said on Monday.

Japan has made steady progress in dealing with its bad loan problems but is still suffering from the after-effects of the bursting of the bubble economy, Honma told a symposium on the international banking system.
The volume of bad loans has declined but their ratio to gross domestic product (GDP) is still high, standing at six percent, he said.

"Further failures (of financial institutions) cannot be ruled out. Major Japanese banks will make arrangements to finish disposing of their bad loans problems within the next one or two years," he said.
Referring to non-bank bad loan problems and the failure last week of Hanwa Bank, he said the monetary authorities would keep close watch and take necessary steps in such cases in future.

On November 20, the Ministry of Finance ordered Hanwa, a second-tier regional bank operating mainly in the Osaka region, to suspend all business except for deposit withdrawals. It said Hanwa's failure to recover bad loans prompted the action.
